transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Stocks opened lower this morning as Pepsi warned of price hikes ahead.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports the Dow Jones industrial average slipped about 13 points in early trading.
Pepsi reported better-than-expected sales for its most recent quarter,
with international shoppers driving much of the gain.
Soda pop and snack food sales in North America were less impressive,
although Pepsi says it's seeing a pickup in demand for healthier-seeming options
such as Lay's baked potato chips and rice cakes.
Pepsi says it plans to raise prices to offset higher costs.
Federal Reserve Governor Chris Waller told an audience in Turkey today
he expects additional hikes in interest rates to calm inflation,
but Waller says there's flexibility about the timing of those moves.
Investors expect the Fed to hold its benchmark interest rates steady
at policymakers' next meeting later this month.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
The aircraft carrier, the USS Abraham Lincoln,
returns to San Diego today after a deployment of 321 days.
It's become a symbol of the war against Iran that has gone on longer than was expected.
Steve Futterman reports from San Diego.
What was supposed to be a six-month mission changed when the U.S. war with Iran began in February.
It was a problem-filled deployment.
There were food and water shortages, difficulties with air conditioning and plumbing.
For some, it was too much.
The Navy confirmed there were a number of suicide attempts.
Yesterday, Secretary of Defense Pete Hexeth flew out to meet the Lincoln.
He thanked the crew and criticized news reports of problems.
There were a few folks in the media who tried to turn the USS Abraham Lincoln
into some sort of a symbol, a symbol of dysfunction.
I know it's the exact opposite.
Hundreds of relatives are expected to be at the naval base to greet the crew.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Futterman in San Diego.
The Canadian poet Anne Carson has won this year's Nobel Prize in Literature.
NPR's Andrew Limbong reports Carson's work blends contemporary poetry
with inspirations from the classics.
The autobiography of Red is Carson's novel in verse reimagining a fragmented ancient Greek poem.
Her book Antigoneck is a postmodern interpretation of Sophocles' Antigoneck.
Carson is a prolific writer, poet, and academic, and her work blurs the lines between the forms.
Here's how Anders Olsson at the Swedish Academy put it.
Almost all her literary production has centered upon the intersection
between the philologist's obsession with words and the poet's desire for new meaning.
The Academy said they'd managed to reach Carson on the phone just moments before the announcement.
Carson said she was in Iceland, quote, "listening to the wind."
Andrew Limbong, NPR News.
The Nobel Peace Prize will be awarded tomorrow.
The Economic Prize will be announced on Monday.
This is NPR.
The National Hurricane Center says its hurricane hunter aircraft
are investigating Hurricane Isaias in the Gulf of Mexico.
Its top sustained winds are at 80 miles per hour.
It's headed for Alabama's Gulf Coast.
Storm watches and warnings are posted from southern Mississippi to the Florida Panhandle.
Forecasters warn Isaias could be very strong when it makes landfall tomorrow.
Student protests continue in France today.
Students have been demonstrating for about three weeks.
They're asking for repairs to dilapidated buildings
and highlighting that there are too few teachers.
The woman who led the team behind the software that helped land astronauts on the moon
has died at the age of 90.
And, Piers Windsor Johnston reports,
Margaret Hamilton's work helped prevent the mission from being aborted.
As Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin descended toward the moon in 1969,
the Apollo 11's computer began flashing alarms, signaling it was overloaded.
But Hamilton's team at MIT had designed the software to draw up less urgent tasks,
allowing the landing to stay on track.
Mission Control gave the astronauts the go-ahead to continue,
and they became the first people to land on the moon.
Hamilton appears in a famous photograph beside a stack of her team's printed code as tall as she was.
She received the Presidential Medal of Freedom from President Barack Obama in 2016,
in a statement MIT remembered her as an inspiration
to generations of engineers whose work helped make the Apollo program a success.
Windsor Johnston, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
This message comes from Jerry.
Many people are overpaying on car insurance.
Why? Switching providers can be a pain.
Jerry helps make the process painless.
Jerry is the only app that compares rates from over 50 insurers in minutes
and helps you switch fast with no spam calls or hidden fees.
Drivers who save with Jerry could save over $1,300 a year.
Before you renew your car insurance policy,

topics.text: Stocks open lower as Pepsi warns of price hikes ahead to offset higher costs
Federal Reserve Governor Chris Waller expects additional interest rate hikes to calm inflation
USS Abraham Lincoln returns to San Diego after 321-day deployment involving war with Iran
Canadian poet Anne Carson wins Nobel Prize in Literature for blending contemporary and classical work
National Hurricane Center investigates Hurricane Isaias in Gulf of Mexico headed for Alabama coast
Student protests continue in France for three weeks over building repairs and teacher shortage
Margaret Hamilton, software engineer behind Apollo 11 moon landing, dies at age 90
